capabilities: Sync notes bi-directionally with a GitHub repository
Sign in via OAuth device flow with token refresh
Push local edits as ordinary commits via the Git Data API
Keep conflict copies when both sides changed a file
Verify written files against Git blob SHAs
disambiguation: Not a Git client wrapper; it speaks the GitHub REST and Git Data APIs over HTTPS, so no Git binary or isomorphic-git is involved.
extras: README states status is early. Tokens are stored in plaintext in the plugin's local.json, which must be excluded from version control and vault sync. A push removing more than 10% of synced files is refused. The in-app mobile test uses Obsidian's emulateMobile and does not cover real iOS networking or file system; the Obsidian-app test runner is macOS only.
intentEvidence: The existing Git plugins shell out to a real Git binary or bundle isomorphic-git, neither of which is a good fit on iOS.
motivation: Obsidian's own sync isn't always an option — some notes live in repositories that can't leave a particular GitHub instance.
problem: Obsidian's built-in sync is not always an option for notes that must stay in a particular GitHub instance, and existing Git plugins rely on a Git binary or isomorphic-git, which do not work well on iOS.

requires.name: GitHub or GitHub Enterprise account with repository access
GitHub App with device flow enabled (required on GitHub Enterprise Server)

summary: Obsidian plugin that syncs notes with a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise Server repository over the GitHub REST API, without a Git binary.
